name: driven single-ion Duffing oscillator (octupole anharmonicity)
question: Does a sweep of the drive frequency remove a branch of the driven ion (threshold write), and with which law?
assumptions: x'' + 2 mu x' + omega0^2 x + alpha x^3 = k cos(omega t) (Akerman 2010 eq. 1), rotating-wave amplitude equations
drive k = 3 mu^{3/2}/sqrt(a) units above the bistability threshold (about 2 for these values)

provenance.source: Akerman, N., Kotler, S., Glickman, Y., Dallal, Y., Keselman, A., Ozeri, R., 'A single-ion nonlinear mechanical oscillator', Phys. Rev. A 82, 061402 (2010), arXiv:1003.1577 (full text)
